A feature release: fan duty on the Motherboard card, and the GPU power limit no longer shows as a warning.

## What changed

- A **Fan duty** section on the Motherboard card shows the PWM duty (percent) the board sends each fan header, under the same names as the fan speed rows. Some fans never report a speed (0 RPM at any duty, for example behind a splitter that does not pass the speed signal on); for them the duty is the only reading. Chips without `pwm` files, such as the ASUS embedded controller, get no duty row. HW Glance still only reads: it never sets fan speeds. When you log all readings, the duty columns are added and a new log file starts.
- **Power limit reached** no longer counts as a warning. Hitting the GPU's power limit is normal operation, but the top bar turned the GPU state red whenever it was Yes. Now only a flag with a limit of its own (thermal throttling) turns anything red or amber; the power limit row still shows Yes or No with its event history, in neutral colours.

The window and the collector speak the same protocol as 0.2.0 (protocol 6). Restart the collector after updating (the step below) so the Fan duty section appears.

The full list is in the [changelog](https://github.com/Raed-Alghamdi/hwglance/blob/v0.3.0/CHANGELOG.md).

## Install or update

Arch Linux, from the package attached below:

```sh
sudo pacman -U hwglance-0.3.0-1-x86_64.pkg.tar.zst
systemctl --user restart hwglanced
sudo systemctl restart hwglance-helper   # if you use the optional helper
hwglance-bar-widget update               # Omarchy only, if you installed the widget
```

For a first install, enable the services instead: `systemctl --user enable --now hwglanced` and, optionally, `sudo systemctl enable --now hwglance-helper`, then `hwglance-bar-widget install` on Omarchy.

Other x86_64 Linux distributions, from the tarball (prebuilt, no Rust needed):

```sh
tar -xzf hwglance-0.3.0-x86_64-linux.tar.gz
cd hwglance-0.3.0-x86_64-linux
./install.sh
```

Check downloads against `SHA256SUMS`. Requirements and optional components are in the [README](https://github.com/Raed-Alghamdi/hwglance#what-you-need).
